It is also possible that once the text of the decree was sent from the Ministry of Justice to the government of the Republic of Croatia, that the working bodies of the government, the coordination bodies or the members of the government itself, added something to the text, because the government could add certain things at its meetings or through the Working Groups. What is clear is that the text which is adopted and which we proposed as the experts who were members of the Working Group did not envisage the transfer of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So you can't remember whether the decree that the Working Group presented to Mr. Separovic to take to the government contained a provision for the transfer of ownership; but you can remember that what the experts of the Working Group proposed was that it did not envisage a transfer of ownership. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I said that we cannot exclude the possibility that within the Working Group this was not discussed. Maybe somebody said that we should see if there was such a constitutional possibility and also that as lawyers we were supposed to see if there were constitutional possibilities for such transfer of ownership or not. I said a few words about that yesterday, what the constitutional provisions are. The constitution does envisage this possibility with compensation, depending on the market value. Also, exceptionally, ownership can be limited but only --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Again, if I can just ask to you focus on the specific questions I ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, the second sentence of the answer reads at this moment: "I said that we cannot exclude the possibility that within the Working Group this was not discussed." Which -- is that the same as that you cannot exclude for the possibility that it was discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. Namely, we are talking about the passing of a law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I think yesterday your testimony that it was never discussed. But I now do understand that - and the English is a bit ambiguous with a double negative - but that you cannot exclude for the possibility that it was discussed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And, Ms. Bagic, you also testified earlier today that you thought it was Mr. Separovic who informed you that a decree on the temporary takeover of property was to be issued, and you thought that that would have been in the second half of August. Now, the Chamber has received evidence that a decision to issue a government decree on the temporary transfer of property with a one-month dead-line for return and repossession was made by President Tudjman at a meeting he held on the 11th of August, 1995, with members of the leadership, including Mr. Radic, Mr. Susak, Mr. Granic, Mr. Valentic, among others, and this is Exhibit P462. Do you know anything about this meeting or the fact that a decision on a decree was being made at this level?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything about this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the views of these various participants at this meeting about the purpose of the property decree and property law were discussed at that meeting. I take it you don't know what those views were, views expressed by Mr. Valentic, Mr. Radic, Mr. Granic, President Tudjman. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're talking about the meeting that you just mentioned that was held at the office of the President of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, on the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, I do not know anything about that meeting, and, therefore, I also do not know anything about the contents of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move on to a slightly different topic, which is the Law on Areas of Special State Concern that you mention in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 3173. And, Your Honour, if I could also tender 65 ter 3D00959, which was the open session of the government on the 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2697. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at paragraph 8, you said: "The Law on Areas for Special State Care and amendments to this law from 2002, Articles 12 and 14, prescribe the time-frames for completing the process of restoring occupancy of property which had been acquired temporarily, pursuant to Law on Temporary Acquisition and Management and the Law on Areas for Special State Care." I take it that you're familiar with this law. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with that law; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And this law was promulgated on the 27th of May, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could look at page 2 of the English and page 1 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And this is Article 2 of the law which states that: "The areas of special state concern shall be determined with the aim of eliminating consequences of the war, for the faster return of displaced persons and refugees, to give impetus to the demographic and economic development, and to achieve as equal development of all areas of ... Croatia as possible." And if we go down to Article 3 of the law, it divides the areas of special state concern into two groups, both of which are areas that were formally occupied. The first group consisting of sparsely populated border areas; and the second group, all other formally occupied territories. And it goes on to set out in detail the municipalities and settlements that come within those areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 7 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S, to part II of this law, which is titled: "Incentive measures for settlement and development of the areas of special state concern."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And Article 7(1) says that the Republic of Croatia shall stimulate the stay and settling of the population in these [sic] areas. And Article 7, paragraph 2, sets out the following categories of population which shall be stimulated in the areas of special state concern. And those categories are then listed, and it includes certain categories of citizens of Croatia, Croatian emigres from abroad, and over the page in the English, Croats expelled from other areas and decide to settle in the Republic of Croatia. And then the last paragraph says that: "These persons shall be considered settlers for the purpose of the law." And if we could look at Article 8, which is there. Article 8(1) says that the ministry of development and reconstruction will issue invitations at least twice a year for the settling of areas of special state concern. Article 8(3) says that the settlers will be given the use of an apartment or family house. Article 8(5) says that the real estate referred to in paragraph 3 shall be allocated for usage pursuant to the decision of the ministry. And if we go over to the next page in English: "And after ten years of settler's continuous occupation of an apartment or a family house in the area of special state concern, it shall become the settler's property."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go down the page in the English and in the B/C/S to Article 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Which sets out the real estate categories of real estate that will be given to the settlers for usage as referred to in Article 8, paragraph 3. And if we go down to the third -- sorry, to sub (2) which is actually mistakenly numbered 3 in the English, it says: "Family houses, that is, the pertinent land in case of a farmer's household or apartments whose owners have abandoned and do not use them in terms of the provisions of the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Administration of Specified Property ..." and it says "... shall be allocated also to the heirs at the proposal of the Ministry and in accordance with the provisions of the said law." And if we turn the page in the English and in the B/C/S as well, it says: "If during the time of its usage the real estate referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article is returned into owner's possession and usage, the ministry shall be obliged to provide the settler with some other adequate apartment or family house, if possible ..." And then the law goes on to describe various tax and salary benefits for those who settle in these areas of special state concern. Now, just to go back to what you said in your statement in paragraph 8, in fact, the original law that was passed in 1996 did not have any time-frames for restoring taken-over property, but it did allow property that had been taken over and given to settlers for their use, that after ten years of occupation, those users would be granted ownership of that property. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. Namely, the Law on Areas of Special State Concern in 1996 in these provisions which you read out, especially the provisions of Article 8, allows that the settlers be given for use the property which was covered by the Law on Temporary Takeover and Management of Property. I referred to time-frames which were in the amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern from the year 2000, firstly, and then from 2002, and which linked up with the later adopted Programme for the Return of Displaced Persons and Refugees and the time frames for repossession that were included there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you may remember from the discussion of the decree at the 31st of August, 1995, closed session, various comments that the ownership of the taken-over property would be dealt with through a separate law and than the normal time-period to be -- allowing ownership to be gained through possession would be shortened. And hereby providing a time-limit of ten years, this cut in half the normal 20-year period for adverse possession under Croatian law. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this Law on Areas of Special State Care, other properties were encompassed, not only the properties dealt with by the Law on Temporary Takeover and Management. This stems from paragraph 3 of Article 9, which prescribes that if a -- the owner returns and repossesses his property for use, which means that it was returned to him, the people living there are entitled to be given other residential facility by the state. This did not refer, this possibility for acquiring ownership did not refer to the property under the Law of Temporary Takeover. I think that in the later amendments to this law adopted in 2002 it was not possible any longer to give this kind of property to settlers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, the -- we discussed already the possibilities for repossession that were in place at this time for Serbs and I am not going to go into that. But the law as it was passed in 1996, the Law on the Areas of Special State Concern, did, in fact, provide for Croats who had been given temporary use of Serb houses to be given ownership of those houses, taken over under the temporary takeover law after ten years, and that was half the normal time-period for adverse possession, right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law allows the possibility for persons, regardless of their ethnicity, and you could read for yourself which particular citizens this referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... why not answer the question? Is the usual term for adverse possession 20 years, and do we find in this law a reduction by half of that time? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, Your Honours, this was not about acquiring ownership rights through adverse possession. So if I enter somebody else's possession in good faith, I can acquire ownership but proving that before the court. Under the law of the areas of state care, certain individuals were given a property for use. After ten years, on that basis, they could acquire ownership. That is what this provision in the law on areas of special state concern reads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in terms of adverse possession, would then the term be 20 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The term for adverse possession under the property law were -- was not changed. If I may, I would just like to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I will allow you to add something. But could you, please, in the follow-up of your examination, start with answering the question and only then give any additional comments you consider of such importance that the Chamber should know. Please make your comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wanted to clarify something. Precisely due to possible different interpretation of this law, the amendments to this law adopted in 2000 included a provision which envisaged that the real estate that was given for use under the provisions of this law, and I'm referring to the Law on Areas of State Care, and the Law on the Takeover of Property and Management, no ownership rights can be acquired through adverse possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask a clarification of one of your previous answers. You said: "After ten years on that basis, they could acquire ownership." That is what this area reads. I read the Article 8: "It shall become the settler's property," as kind of an almost automatic consequence. Which seems not to be exactly the same as that you could acquire but that you would acquire ownership, because it's a "shall" disposition, but that's the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But what I wanted to underline, on that basis, was that those individuals who were given these properties had to have a decision issued by a competent body granting them the use of a certain real estate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, you keep referring to the amendments, and I will -- we will look at the 2000 amendments, so I'd like to you put those aside for the moment and focus on this 1996 law. And because I'm not sure I got a very clear answer to this, I'm going to ask again that the properties given to settlers for their use under this law and in which they could acquire ownership after ten years of occupancy included properties taken over under the temporary takeover law, right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my understanding an interpretation of this law, the properties encompassed by the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Management of Properties could not become the property to -- of the persons to whom it was allocated for use under this law.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what specific provisions are you relying on when you draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I rely my conclusions on the fact that this was the property owned by other individuals. When we talk about the Law on Temporary Takeover, that was the property of natural persons. Under this law, it could have been given for temporary use, which was done. However, this law also provides for a possibility for giving this property for temporary use to settlers in the areas covered by the Law on State Care. I also base my conclusion on paragraph 3 which speaks about the return of owners, and it stipulates that such returnees can claim their ownership or repossession. It says that anyone can -- stripped of their ownership, that can be done only according to market value of the property. That was in line with the constitution of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, what seems to be the question is that Article 8, paragraph 5, talking about acquiring ownership after an occupancy of ten years, does not make any distinction in relation to where that property comes from, whether it was privately owned previously, whether it belonged to a company. It just says, Once you've given the usage, once the property has been allocated for usage pursuant to the decision of the ministry, then after ten years, the settler shall obtain ownership. Now, you're telling us that if the owner has, meanwhile, requested repossession, then that may be different. Then, of course, there will be no uninterpreted usage of ten years at least, once it has been made effective. But where in this law do we find that the user, that the settler, who has used the property for ten years will not become the owner if it is property which was put under the state administration as a result of the Law on the Temporary Takeover? Could you tell us where we find that in this law? Because that apparently is your answer to Ms. Gustafson's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, indeed, cannot be found in this law, because it is not stated as such explicitly in the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, something else is stated explicitly, that is, that after ten years of use, that you shall become the settler's property. That's what the law says rather explicit. What's -- do you have any case law or is there any other source which you can invoke in order to contradict what clearly seems to be the text of this piece of legislation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I already mentioned something in that respect. First of all, the constitution of the Republic of Croatia, the Law on Property and other substantive rights, and the Law on the Temporary Takeover and management of properties followed by amendments to the Law on Special areas -- of state care. Why am I saying this? Because the law on special areas of state care covered much more properties in comparison to those encompassed by the Law on Temporary Takeover and Management. It included the state-owned property; that is to say, that used to be socially owned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you are repeating part of your previous answer, that this law covers other property as well. But, I just pointed the text of this law, which does not make any distinction in this respect. Now, you invoked the constitution. Is this to say that the unlimited language of Article 8 means that this language or this text violates the constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because it included other types of properties that was not owned by physical persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And besides that, I already said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you say is to some extent in other respects it may not be unconstitutional. I want to focus on property allocated for use to settlers which was private property which was covered by the Law on Temporary Takeover. I want to focus on that exclusively. As we see, Article 8 makes no distinction and apparently does not exclude those properties from becoming the settler's property after ten years of use. Now, you say, It's the constitution which contradicts, that this is how we have to read this Article. Does it mean that, in respect of this type of property, that Article 8, not making any distinctions, is, in this respect, unconstitutional?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, Your Honours, might be perceived in that way. However, that would be our perception of that provision, because the constitutionality of this provision was not disputed by the constitutional court and therefore the court did not abolish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know how to proceed because I do want to draw the Chamber's attention to something in the law, but I don't know if it's appropriate to do it in front of the witness, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would be inappropriate to do it in the presence of the witness. We are close to a break. Perhaps once we take the break that -- That's exactly your answer, where you invoked the constitution as -- of guidance, how to read this. And that I asked you whether there is any case law and you say this is, however, constitutionality or unconstitutionality is not to be found in any decision of the constitutional court. Now, the other reason why we had not to read Article 8 as I did, the Law on Property and other substantive rights, you said, was another reason why we could not read that Article 8 would also give ownership. It would give the property of privately owned property to settlers who had used it for more than ten years. Could you give us any specific part of that law which would be of guidance in interpreting Article 8, paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I'm referring to the general provisions of this law, stipulating the inalienability of the property law, and it provides only for compensation according to the market value of the property, in case of seizure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say that that's a provision which almost prohibits what was said here. We have looked at the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Management. Thank you for those answers. Ms. Gustafson, I interrupted. We're close to where we need a break. Mr. Misetic would like to draw our attention to a specific portion of this law. Would you -- nevertheless, would you want to find a more appropriate moment, or would this be an appropriate moment for a break?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This is an appropriate moment, Your Honour. And if I could also get an exhibit number for this law before we break, that would be helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2698. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2698 is admitted into evidence. Ms. Bagic, the break starts already for you. We'd like to see you back in a little bit over 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it's new evidence, so therefore we might not be that familiar yet with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I might not be, myself, Mr. President. But Article 10 of the law --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Article 10, let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I note right at the outset that the original of Article 10 is different in its numbering from the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just find it first. I have Article 10 there front of me, which starts with the real estate given to the settlers for their --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then you will note in the English there are three -- four subparagraphs, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. Yes, although we have a bit of an odd numbering. From the English version, Article 10 starts with a one between brackets; then we have 1, 2, 3; and then on the next page in e-court, page 10 out of 23, we have a 3 in brackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe in the original, if you look, and this will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If would you give me an opportunity to look at it for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters would be grateful if we could have the relevant Article on the screen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have Article 10 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One page prior in the original and one page prior in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the original, apparently, Article 10 starts with a one between brackets then two paragraphs numbered 1 and 2. Then it follows with a 2 between brackets and then there is an third between brackets, paragraph on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the -- at least, in the translation, the numbering is confusing; and -- but I take it that you didn't only want to take us to the numbering but also to the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Now, if we look at Article 10, it describes what real estate will be given to settlers, referred to in Article 8, paragraph 3. And then in -- numbered -- in the original bracketed number 2, which is, in this version of the English translation, number 3, talks about family houses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- et cetera under the Law on the Temporary Takeover. Then if we go to the last paragraph of this Article -- If we could turn the page, please, in both Croatian and English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I read this to be that if the property is allocated for usage to a settler, that if during the time of its usage that the property is returned into the owner's possession that then the minister is under an obligation to find alternative accommodation for the settler.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but besides that. Because of the -- well, there's two issues I wanted to raise. One is, I think, due to the misnumbering in the English, in the original, this paragraph refers to property from the temporary takeover law. And then the second issue it was unclear to me whether usage only means within a ten-year period or it could mean after that. So I don't know when the witness was referring to within the provisions of the law. It was contemplated that people would be getting this property back. This may have been something that she may have wished to comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the whole system of the Law on the Temporary Takeover and reclaiming the possession and usage of property seems to be based on a continued existence of ownership of the original owner. Whereas, if, under this law, after ten years of usage, you obtain ownership, then I, at least, have some difficulties in understanding how that could be dealt with by just returning them into the owner's possession and usage where he apparently has lost his ownership unless you would accept a kind of dual ownership. But it's -- first of all, I think it was for was the witness to explain that, and your possible explanation, at least on my mind, raises more questions than it resolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if I could just explain my position, Mr. President. First just that the witness didn't have the law in front of her at the time when she was being asked to locate within the law what provisions she may have been relying on in explaining that return of the property was contemplated within the law. So that's -- that's the first issue. The second issue in the overall context, just to address the point that you were raising, is that it's not confiscation of property if, A, the person retains ownership, but, B, there's also the second portion which is for adequate compensation. So in terms of what was put to this witness, if, after ten years somebody would get ownership of the property through, it wouldn't be, in my view, adverse possession but a form of eminent domain, then if that original owner received compensation, then it still wouldn't be confiscation of property. But that's just to address the remark that you made, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that that's your interpretation, your view on the matter. Ms. Gustafson, since it was to some extent argumentative, would you like to add anything at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, except to say that we will request a revision of the translation to amend the numbering of this provision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That at least avoids quite a bit of confusion. We will have a break, and we will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, my first question is whether you're ready to proceed; second question is how much time you would still think you would need.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I would like to finish in this session. I'm not sure, in light of how long it has taken to get through some topics so far, if I can manage. But that is my goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Bagic, could I invite you to focus your answers on the questions that are put to you as much as possible. Ms. Gustafson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have 65 ter 689 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, the document that is about to come up on the screen are the 2000 amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern that you have mentioned several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that there are some technical difficulties which are expected to be fixed soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: There we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Bagic, can you see from the decision proclaiming this law into force that it was -- that this amendment was made after President Tudjman had died and Mr. Mesic became president. And at the bottom of the English we see Article 1 of this amendment. And the first amendment is that Article 2 of the 1996 law is changed, and the wording "displaced persons and refugees," is replaced with the wording "population which inhabited those areas before the homeland war." So whereas the stated aims of defining the areas of special state concern in 1996 was included the faster return of displaced persons and refugees with this 2000 amendment, the aim was changed to the faster return of population which inhabited those areas before the homeland war.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 5 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S, to Article 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This Article erases Articles 6 and 7 of the 1996 law, and you may recall that Article 7 of that law set out the categories of populations which were subject to the measures to stimulate stay and settling, including Croatian emigres and Serbian and Bosnian Serb Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 6 of this law, this amends Article 8. And if we turn the page in the English, Article 8(1).

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Which used to state that the ministry of development and reconstruction would issue invitations for settling the areas of special state concern. Now Article 8 -- 8(1) states that Croatia will promote the return and stay of the population which lived in areas of special state concern before the homeland war as well as the settling of Croatian citizens who can contribute to economic and social development?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page in the English and page 4 of the B/C/S, to Article 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This amends Article 10 of the 1996 law, which you'll recall was the provisions setting out the categories of property which could be allocated to settlers. And you can see that it removes the category of houses that had been taken over under the temporary takeover law.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we go to page 8 in the English, the next page in the English and in the B/C/S to Article 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And this provision requires the ministry to repeal decisions on use of property under this law "which pertain to the property owned by natural persons." And that would be a reference to property that had been taken over under the temporary takeover law, right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but also, in accordance to this law, the Law on Areas of Special State Concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And on the next page in the English, Article 14, this states that properties allocated for temporary use to other persons pursuant to the provisions of this law "shall be returned into the owner's possession within six months ... of the submission of a request by [sic] the owner of the property." And then it sets out certain procedures. And if we go to the next page in the English, Article 16 states at the top of that page: "The right of acquiring ownership over another's property through possession shall not be obtained over the real estate unit owned by natural persons allocated for use under this law, the Law on Temporary Takeover and Administration of Specified Property ... and the Law on the Lease of Apartments in the liberated territory [sic]." Now, this amendment in 2000, this was the first time that that this law, the Law on Areas of Special State Concern, provided mechanisms for return of property temporarily taken over under the temporary takeover law. I'm not talking about amendments to the temporary takeover law, I'm talking about this law, the Law on Areas of Special State Concern.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood properly, you're referring to the amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern. It is correct that these amends to the law - there was another set of amendments later in 2002 - but these were the amendments that had to do with regulating the issue of returning for possession the property that was allocated for use in accordance with the Law on Areas of Special State Concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And when I was asking you before about settlers who had been granted property that this been taken over under the temporary takeover law, having -- being granted ownership of that property after ten years, in accordance with the 1996 law, this 2000 amendment changed that by stating that those settlers could not acquire ownership of property taken over under the temporary takeover law through possession. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this had to do with adverse possession and this is the provision that we can see on the screen. It is a provision of Article 16 that the right of acquiring ownership could not exist only through adverse possession. I said earlier that adverse possession existed when someone would be using property owned by somebody else without any sort of regulation or act by which this was allocated for use, but here it's explicitly provided, though that followed from the basic provisions of the basic Law on Property. That's the Law on Property and other material rights. But as for this law it here referred to the property of persons who had abandoned it and that was used -- allocated for use to others, then the procedure was specified here in the provisions of Article 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And these amendments to this law in particular, removing property that had been temporarily taken over under the temporary takeover law from the provisions of this law, and introducing the concept that the law would aim at the faster return of population that inhabited those areas before the homeland war, and would encourage the return and stay of the population which lived in those areas before the homeland war, those changes reflected a policy change of the Croatian authorities; whereas, previously, the authorities had focussed on encouraging Croats to move into the areas affected by Operations Storm and Flash. As this amendment reflects, at this time, they were also taking steps to promote the -- or facilitate the return of Serbs who used to live in those areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But please allow me to add something as well. One of the purposes of the Law on Areas of Special State Concern from 1996 was, inter alia, the settlement of Croats. That is correct, and this provision does not exist in the amendment from the year 2000. However, simultaneously, while the Law on Areas of Special State Concern was in force, and as it referred to the temporary takeover and management of certain property, in the meantime the Programme for the Return of Displaced Persons, Expelled Persons, and Refugees was also adopted, and it referred to the procedures for repossessing property that was covered by the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Management of certain property. And this programme, as is well known, was adopted in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We're actually going to look at that programme briefly in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could tendered this document, 65 ter 689, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2699. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2699 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, you looked at the return -- you were shown the return programme yesterday, and we can bring it up if you -- if we need to. But I just wanted to ask you this: That programme, which is Exhibit D428, created a commission for the implementation of the return programme, and it states that the deputy minister of justice was to be a member of that commission. And you were, at the time, the deputy minister of justice, and so my question is: Were you a member of that commission?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the deputy minister of justice, and, on the basis of my function, I was a member of this commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could look at D420, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The document that is about to come up is a report from the year 2000 on the implementation of the Programme of Return by the commission for the implementation for the return programme. Do you remember being involved, as a member of that commission, in drafting a report of this nature in 2000?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that I directly participated in that, because the burden of this issue of the refugees and expelled persons and their return was with the ministry of the development and reconstruction and the administration for refugees and expelled persons. But as for what was within the remit of work of the Ministry of Justice and possible objections to this report, it was probably submitted to me so that I could provide my opinions, suggestions, and possible objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to page 20 of the English and page 18 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And, at the top of that page, the title is: "Restitution of property, housing commissions." And it says: "The main problem in the implementation of the Programme of Return is the restitution of property, i.e., work of the Housing Commission [sic] in charge of resolving restitution of property, whose owners are mostly refugees, currently in FRY and BiH, which is a consequence of the implementation of the Law on Temporary Sequester of Private Property in the Republic of Croatia." Do you recall this conclusion by the commission in the year 2000 that even two years after the Law on the Temporary Takeover had been repealed that the legacy of that law remained -- was the main problem in implementing the Programme of Return?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the facts behind this conclusion at this point in time. But it is a fact that the -- there were issues with the restitution of property. It was a complex issue, and that was why there were various solutions in the legislation. They were changed over time, and this issue remained important after the year 2000. One of the reasons it was also to change the Law on Areas of Special State Concern in 2002. And the work of the Housing Commissions was especially important because it turned out that the Housing Commissions, in spite of the original purpose, should be the main stakeholders, that they should be mainly in charge of implementing all this. They had to list the property and do everything else. And for a number of reasons, they were very often not able or capable to implement all that they were expected to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 28 in the English and page 25 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in the middle of the page in the English there's a section called: Amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern. Which is around the middle of the page in the B/C/S. And the second half of this introductory paragraph says: "Amendments to this law are under way, primarily related to the elimination of discriminatory provisions in the part of the law referring to the allocation of property to settlers, first of all, houses, according to the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Management of Specified Property, which has been invalidated." Now, as the deputy minister of justice, were you involved in this aspect of the report or the work of the commission; namely, eliminating discriminatory provisions in the Law on Areas of Special State Concern?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, from which year and from what date is this report? From the year 2000, but could you please show the first page so that we could see the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It says 2000, and I'm not sure there is a more specific date. I'll check.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: There doesn't appear to be.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] I'm asking that because my duty as the deputy justice minister was terminated in January 2000 so that until that point in time, I participated in the work of this commission as the deputy justice minister, and I participated, as I said, in the segments that had to do with the remit of work of the Ministry of Justice. After that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the cover page says April 2000, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I apologise; it does. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which might not be of great impact where the witness said that she finished her job as a deputy minister of justice in January 2000. But the report is of April 2000.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At the time, I was no longer the deputy justice minister, so, therefore, I did not [as interpreted] participate in the work of this commission or in the drafting of the report. Maybe I did with some earlier ones, because, at the time, I was head of the legislation office of the Government of the Republic of Croatia, and later on, I did participate in the work of a joint work group which -- of the Government of the Republic of Croatia, which comprised representatives of the government, including representatives of various ministries, as well as the international community, such as the UNHCR, OSCE, and the European Commission. And we worked on the amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern which came into force in 2002. And the purpose was to terminate the procedure of restitution of property which had been temporarily taken over in accordance with the Law on Temporary Takeover and Management of certain property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, one intervention just for the sake of the clarity of the transcript. This is page 74, line 8 when witness was referring that she was no longer the deputy justice minister so therefore she did -- one word is missing, obviously, before the verb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could verify. You referred to that you may have possibly have been involved in some earlier reports, but you said: "And later on ..." you did -- did you say you "did" or you "did not" participate in the work of a joint work group which comprised representatives of the government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did participate in its work, and I was also co-chairman of this work group, which was established by the Government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, that we have some misunderstanding. I will read line 7 on page 74.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Yes, at that time I was no longer the deputy justice minister, so, therefore, I did ... participate in the work of this commission." She was no longer deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, participated. That's -- yes. Please proceed, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And yesterday you were asked questions about the reason behind the abolition of the Law on the Temporary Takeover of Property in 1998 and the enactment of mechanisms for repossession in the return programme in 1998, and you've just explained that you were involved in amendments to the Law on Areas of Special State Concern. The Chamber has received evidence that the elimination or amendment of these laws that related to property of Serbs, Croatian Serbs and their return, that those changes were made under significant pressure by the -- by members of the international community. Is that consistent with your recollection, or are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. As I said, I was directly involved in that. From the level at which I participated in the amendments to this law, I cannot speak about pressure from the international community. That was a joint Working Group. Before the group met, the ministry representatives and representatives of international community would meet in order to consider the implementation of various regulations. Our objective was, after difficult experiences, to finally, after several years, bring this Programme of Return to an end. The situation was complex; it was difficult to obtain data; and there were extensive debates professional, legal, and practical about that. But I wouldn't characterise that as pressure. We discussed the practical aspect of certain issues. I think that it was in 2001, there were 4.000 empty houses from which the temporary users had been removed. However, the rightful owners were inaccessible and an agreement was reached to try through the UNHCR and the Serbian democratic forum to contact those owners form whom we supposed were in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I just want to focus back to my question which was about pressure from the international community. And in your answer you said at first I cannot speak about pressure from the international community. And then you said later on -- later on you said: "But I wouldn't characterise that as pressure." Were you involved at the political level on return issues with anyone from the international community? Are you able to speak about the extent to which members of the international community were pressuring Croatia on return?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not personally take part while I was in the legislation office in those political discussions. I was in regular contact with experts and representatives of international community from the organisations that I mentioned, with a view to removing obstacles to the return of refugees and other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could to 65 ter 7520, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It should be available now. Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, the document that is going to appear on your screen is a report from December of 2002 by the International Crisis Group, and this was at the time when you were the head of the legislative office for the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of the English and page 2 of the partial translation. If we could go to the very bottom of the page in the English on the left-hand side and to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the sentence that begins right at the bottom of the page in the English and near the top in the B/C/S: "A 1998 government return programme failed to establish adequate conditions. The effects of discriminatory laws and practices put in place during and after the war continued to prevent them from exercising their rights in key areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. Could we have some foundation what is it International Crisis Group? I mean, whether witness is familiar with this group or -- could we have some foundation on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please take care of that in your questioning, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think when I ask the question, it will -- I mean, it will be clear that there's no -- I mean, I'm going to ask her about the contents of what is said; it's not particularly the group. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The author of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to put to a witness a certain document in which opinions are expressed then, of course, it is important to know who expressed those opinions. Just -- otherwise you can, of course, ask questions about the matter as such. But if you use a text, it should be clear where it comes from, what the authority of it is -- that, for example, if the witness would know that this group consisted of certain people she knows who failed their exams at university, for example, that it might be interesting to hear such comments. Therefore, you are invited to pay proper attention to that aspect of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In light of the time, Your Honour, I will not use this document and, in fact, have no further questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. Mr. Mikulicic, I'm looking at the clock, and I have not yet consulted with my colleagues. Would have you further questions for the witness, and how much time would that take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will only have a couple of questions, and I think I could manage to go through them within next at least ten -- at most ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then I have to look at the court schedule for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then with the indulgence of transcribers, technicians, interpreters, you have ten minutes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will try to be even shorter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Bagic, just a few questions. I will not keep you too long. The Chamber asked you to interpret the fact due to which the agreement on normalisation was concluded solely with the FRY, the agreement which regulated certain issues relating to the sequester of property.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For that purpose, can we please have on the screen Exhibit D1761.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is the legislative document of the Former Republic of Serbia and Krajina, which stipulates that all citizens of the Serbian Krajina were also registered as citizens of the FRY. In view of such legal status and regardless of where the citizens of the Serbian Krajina were, whether they be in Italy or in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or anywhere else, according to your legal understanding, is it usual and normal to conclude such an agreement with their homeland?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seemed a logical move.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: My learned friend, the Prosecutor, has just shown you document D428, which is the programme of return and providing of -- for the return of refugees and IDPs dating from 1998. In order to be expeditious, I would just refer you to a provision in this document which in item 4 says that the government reiterates its obligation undertaken with a view to implementing the right of owners for repossession and free disposal of property. According to your understanding, this position expressed in an official document of the Croatian parliament in 1998, does it govern the issue of ownership of the property that was under the Law of Temporary Takeover was placed under the state sequester?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA BAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does because the programme explicitly refers, particularly in, I think, items 9 and 14, to the property taken over under the Law on the Temporary Takeover and Management of Properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: My last question: In principle, when we consider a specific legal situation, especially within the context of a state that is just developing its state system, is it possible to interpret a legal situation based on a single regulation, or is your experience something completely different?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question is -- it is totally vague and, I mean, I just I don't think there's any basis for this. It just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will withdraw my question, Your Honour, and have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you earlier raised a matter which seems not to be urgent anymore, perhaps also in view of the subsequent amendments which we discussed with the witness. So, therefore, I take it that there is no need for further questions. Ms. Gustafson, have the -- has the re-examination of the witness triggered any need ...

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bagic, then this concludes your testimony, since the Bench has no questions for you, or I should say has no further questions for you. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by parties and by the Bench. And I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just abuse for one second the circumstances that we would have one or two minutes extra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to put two things on the record. The first is that an extension of deadlines was granted for filings during the Christmas recess. As previously indicated to the parties in an e-mail, the Chamber extended deadlines for responses to motions filed during the period of the 21st of December, 2009, through 8 of January, 2010, to three weeks. That's put on the record, it was informally communicated with the parties in an e-mail which was sent on the 18th of December, 2009, at 5.41 p.m. I further, for full transparency, would like to inform the parties that, a bit unusual, but the Chamber received from a witness who testified here, Mr. Drazen Vitez, a book under the title of "Varazdin," that Chamber considers that this book, which is of a touristic character, a lot of nice pictures, and Varazdin being quite far away from the area covered by the indictment, that it is intended as a gift for the Tribunal. We do not know whether the library has any place for such books. If not -- and I understood that others were provided with a copy of this as well. But as soon as the Chamber receives anything which looks like a gift, it should be put on the record. I had a look at it. It is a nice book. I can't read the text, so don't worry about it. That having been put on the record, Mr. Mikulicic, will you have your next witness ready tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that will be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That will be expert witness Mr. General Repinc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And an arrangement has been made in relation to cross-examination of this witness, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. My learned colleague from the OTP asks if the cross-examination could start on Monday because Ms. Prashanthi is temporarily away due to personal reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And this informal request was granted until now. Did I -- was I informed that you would need four to five sessions with the expert witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other parties would need some time with cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I informed my co-counsel that we would be one to two sessions, but I think we will be approximately no more than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And we will be likewise one session, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that we would have ended up most likely to start the cross-examination with the OTP not any earlier than on Friday, and, therefore, that the decision to allow the Prosecution to start its cross-examination Monday is not of dramatic consequences. We adjourn, and thanking the interpreters, transcribers, technicians, security, for allowing the witness to be further excused. We'll adjourn and we resume on Wednesday, the 13th of January, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
